source: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) — monetary policy instruments workbook
license: MNB public data; robots.txt on www.mnb.hu is a single '*' group disallowing only /archivum/ — this path is permitted
replaces: the HUF leg of a paid central-bank-balance-sheet / official-flow product (Macrobond, Haver, CEIC class)
cadence: DAILY (the SNB sight-deposit analogue is WEEKLY — this is 5x the resolution on the same mechanism)
verification: VERIFIED AS DATA, MECHANISM CLAIM RETRACTED IN-RUN. First pass 'verified' a -28.3% drop on 2022-10-14 (the MNB emergency-hike day, EURHUF all-time high). Re-checking the surrounding path KILLED that claim: the series steps 266 -> 4013 HUF bln between 2022-09-29 and 2022-10-06 and daily swings of +93%/-12% are routine inside that week, so the crisis-day move is a coincidence inside an administrative transition. Monthly medians expose THREE clean step-changes -- 2022-10 (+823%), 2023-04 (+96%), 2023-10 (+192%) -- matching the MNB's published reserve-ratio increases. The series is therefore real and correctly parsed (the steps ARE the policy history, which is the ground-truth confirmation), but its variance is dominated by RESERVE-REQUIREMENT POLICY, not by official FX flow. Independent internal control that does hold: the 'quick depo' sheet spans 2022-10-14 -> 2023-09-29, matching the published life of the emergency instrument.
known_failure_modes: POSITIONAL-COLUMN TRAP: 'standing facilities', 'quick depo' and 'long term deposit' carry a SECOND DATE column (maturity) in position B. A reader taking columns [0,1] as (date,value) returns Excel date serials (44849) as billions of HUF — large, plausible, monotone, and it raises no error. Key on the cell reference letter, and read the bilingual header rows 5/6.
SPARSE CELLS: blank cells are omitted from the XML entirely, so a positional reader shifts columns on any row with a gap. Same fix.

WEEKEND FILL-FORWARD: reserve balances repeat the Friday value on Sat/Sun (2022-10-15 == 2022-10-16 == 2909.511). A naive daily-difference feature emits a structural zero on weekends and a 3-day change on Mondays.

SHEET-ORDER TRAP (mine, not theirs): xl/worksheets/sheet10.xml sorts before sheet2.xml lexicographically, so sorted(namelist) mislabels 11 of 13 sheets. Resolve names through xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels, never by sorting filenames.

MIXED ACTIVE/INACTIVE: rows 'Active instruments -->' and 'Inactive instruments -->' are EMPTY divider sheets; 6 of the 13 series are discontinued instruments (2w depo ends 2016-04, 3m depo 2018-12, preferential deposit 2022-04, 1w depo 2022-10, quick depo 2023-09, long term deposit 2023-12). A survivorship-blind consumer joins live and dead instruments into one panel.
The workbook is REPUBLISHED IN PLACE at one URL with no version stamp — revisions are silent. Archive each pull (Bronze).

ADMINISTRATIVE-POLICY CONTAMINATION (the finding, and the third instance of this class in three institutions after the SNB/Credit-Suisse and CNB/instrument-mix cases): the raw reserve balance and its differences are NOT an intervention proxy. The largest moves in the series are reserve-requirement changes. Same shape as the SNB sight-deposit series being contaminated by the Credit Suisse rescue -- an official-sector series whose biggest moves are plumbing, not flow.
reconstruction: The usable official-flow quantity is EXCESS reserves = daily reserve-account balance minus the MONTHLY required reserve (the 'reserve requirements' sheet, 236 months 2007-01 -> 2026-08). This is the construction a vendor charges for and it is computable entirely from this one free file. It removes the 2022-10 and 2023-04 administrative breaks (+823% -> +182 HUF bln, +96% -> +42). HONEST RESIDUAL: the 2023-10 break SURVIVES the normalisation (-689 -> +6293 HUF bln), so the requirement sheet does not capture whatever changed that month. Any consumer must carry a structural-break dummy at 2023-10 or start the sample after it.
excess_reserves_note: daily balance minus that calendar month's required reserve; n=7060
